punchline: Harari's twist on the farming revolution: wheat domesticated us, and the people tending it ended up working harder and eating worse.
thirty_sec: Harari calls the Agricultural Revolution history's biggest fraud. A wild grass in the Middle East, wheat, ended up growing across the world, and the people who tended it cleared stones, weeded, dug canals and wore out their spines. Villages grew, but diets got poorer and at least one child in three died before twenty. Nobody walked back, because every extra comfort had become a necessity.
